result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edge clustering coefficient for specified edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10658-L10791){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient( edge_ids=None, k=3, normalize=True, offset=True ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The edge clustering coefficient measures how "clustered" the neighborhood around an edge is, based on k-cycles (cycles of length k) the edge participates in. For `k=3` (triangles): - counts triangles containing the edge - maximum possible: `min(d_i - 1, d_j - 1)` where `d_i`, `d_j` are endpoint degrees - value of `1.0` means edge is in a complete subgraph For `k=4` (4-cycles): - counts 4-cycles containing the edge - maximum possible: `(d_i - 1)(d_j - 1)` - measures "squareness" of edge neighborhood ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of edge IDs (integers) to compute coefficient for. If `None`, computes for all edges. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Cycle size to use. Must be `3` (triangles) or `4` (4-cycles). [normalize]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to normalize by maximum possible cycles given endpoint degrees. If `False`, returns raw cycle count. [offset]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to add `1` to cycle count (original Radicchi et al. definition). When `offset=True`: `C(e) = (z + 1) / s`. When `offset=False`: `C(e) = z / s`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mapping from edge ID (integer) to clustering coefficient. With `normalize=True`: range `[0, 1+]` (can exceed `1` with offset). With `normalize=False`: raw cycle count. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If k is not 3 or 4. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Complexity: - k=3: O(|V| d log d + |E| d) where d is max degree - k=4: O(|V| d log d + |E| d²) The original Radicchi et al. definition uses `normalize=True` and `offset=True`. Setting `offset=False` allows the normalized metric to reach exactly `1.0` for edges in complete subgraphs. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Triangle graph (complete graph K3): ::: {#a1cb507e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) # All edges are in 1 triangle ecc = graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, normalize=True, offset=True) # Each edge: (1 triangle + 1) / min(2-1, 2-1) = 2/1 = 2.0 # Without offset ecc = graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, normalize=True, offset=False) # Each edge: 1 / 1 = 1.0 (maximum clustering) ``` ::: Square graph (4-cycle): ::: {#02f456a7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") .add_edge("D", "A") ) # k=3: No triangles ecc3 = graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, offset=False) # All edges: 0.0 (no triangles) # k=4: Each edge participates in 1 four-cycle ecc4 = graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=4, offset=False) # Edge A-B: 1 / ((2-1)*(2-1)) = 1.0 ``` ::: Karate club network: ::: {#2a490bca .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ec.karate_club() # Get k=3 edge clustering for all edges ecc = G.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, normalize=True, offset=False) # Find edges with highest clustering (most embedded in triangles) sorted_edges = sorted(ecc.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True) # Returns top 5 edges by clustering sorted_edges[:5] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [(50, 1.0), (56, 1.0), (68, 1.0), (49, 1.0), (11, 1.0)] ``` ::: :::
